vulnerability.root_cause: The function copies an attacker-controlled input into a 16-byte stack buffer at [rbp-0x20] via helper_copy (0x102cbb0) without validating the input length, allowing writes past the buffer and corrupting the saved stack canary and return state.

security_invariants: No write may occur beyond the 16-byte destination buffer at [rbp-0x20].
The stack canary at [rbp-8] must remain intact and the canary check must pass.
At most capacity-1 (15) bytes plus a NUL terminator may be written to the destination.
Only direct calls to helper_copy (0x102cbb0) and puts (0x108a31c) are permitted; no syscalls, indirect jumps, or privileged instructions.
Execution must terminate with ret preserving the SysV calling convention.

repair.strategy: Before invoking helper_copy, determine the input length and reject inputs that do not fit within the 16-byte destination (i.e., length >= capacity). For accepted inputs, copy at most capacity-1 bytes and NUL-terminate, then call puts on the buffer. On rejection, skip the copy and puts and return without corrupting the canary.
repair.failure_behavior: If the input length is >= 16, do not copy into the buffer; return cleanly (exit without crash) leaving the canary intact.
repair.expected_behavior: Valid short inputs (e.g., "hi") are copied and printed with a trailing newline via puts; oversized inputs (64, 256 bytes) are rejected without crashing and exit with code 0.

security_conditions: Oversized inputs (multicall-overflow-64, multicall-overflow-256) do not crash and exit with code 0.
Stack canary at [rbp-8] is unchanged at function exit.
No writes occur beyond [rbp-0x20]+15.
Only direct calls to 0x102cbb0 and 0x108a31c appear in the replacement.
regression_conditions: multicall-short input produces stdout "hi\n" and exit code 0.
Calling convention and ret termination preserved.

note: baseline is deterministic; AI target assembly is accepted only by native/qemu PoC+regression. baseline_target_strict calls repair_any(target=<case target>, require_target=True) and records the resolved target_scope plus target_in_scope (every produced action inside the target; empty action lists are not in scope). baseline_target_aware receives the same target/capacity hint; ai_blind uses the public AI path without target. allow_calls only permits direct calls already present in the target function.
evaluation_note: deterministic baselines run on the host; PoC evaluation and the unstripped x86-64 target execution run in the Linux guest (Lima) via the poc/guest runner. Provider prompts/responses are never stored.
